tools.name: help
tools.description: Show the user a curated menu of what they can ask this memoQ assistant to do. ALWAYS call this when the user asks what they can do, what you can do, what commands or tools are available, or asks for help - then present the returned card verbatim (it is Markdown). It also explains the one thing that surprises everyone: translations are STAGED, not written, and reach memoQ when the user runs Pre-translate.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: What the plugin knows about the memoQ project: language pair, client/domain/subject, each captured document with its segment and confirmed-pair counts, and how many translations are currently staged. The plugin only sees what memoQ sends it - if this comes back empty, ask the user to run Pre-translate once (any model, even a cheap one) or visit some segments, and the picture fills in.

tools.name: get_segments
tools.description: The document's segments. With the Supervertaler preview tool running this is the LIVE view from memoQ: rows in real order, each with source, current target text, a partId, and isActive on the cursor row. Without it, it is what the plugin has captured from translation requests (source only, in the order memoQ sent them). Use offset/limit to page through long documents. TAGS: Reproduce whatever markup arrives in the source, byte for byte, wherever it belongs in the target. The forms depend on memoQ's import filter and vary between projects: and are common, ... and ... occur, and an HTML element can arrive as several spec_char tags rather than one. Placeholders are not consistent either - {0} may arrive as a tag while %1 arrives as literal text - so never normalise or rewrite markup, and never assume a form you have seen before. GROUND TRUTH: after a Pre-translate, get_project lists a captured-requests document (origin 'translation requests'); get_segments on that key returns the exact strings memoQ asked for, each marked with whether it is staged. That is the only view that shows how memoQ actually split the text, and it is the view to verify against.

document.description: Document key from get_project. Omit for the most recently active document.

tools.name: get_active_segment
tools.description: Where the user's cursor is in memoQ right now. Returns the paragraph (part) it is in with full source and target, plus activeSource/activeTarget: the sentence within that paragraph that is actually selected – the memoQ grid row – when the paragraph has several. Needs the Supervertaler preview tool running (memoQ starts it automatically once registered); if it is not, this says so. Use before requests such as 'translate this one' or 'what does this segment say'.

tools.name: go_to_segment
tools.description: Ask memoQ to select a segment, by index (from get_segments) or by part id. Units from get_segments are paragraphs; to land on one sentence of a multi-sentence paragraph, pass sourceStart/sourceLength = that sentence's character range within the paragraph's source. Needs the Supervertaler preview tool running. Moves the user's cursor, so use it when they asked to be taken somewhere, not as a side effect of reading.

partId.description: Alternatively the exact part id from get_segments / get_active_segment.

document.description: Document GUID or name when several are open. Omit for the most recently active.

sourceStart.description: Optional: 0-based start of the sentence within the paragraph's source text.

tools.name: check_numbers
tools.description: QA check over the live document: paragraphs whose numbers differ between source and target (digits compared with thousand/decimal separators stripped, so 1.234,56 matches 1,234.56). Only translated paragraphs are checked. Needs the Supervertaler preview tool running. Each issue carries an index usable with go_to_segment.

document.description: Document GUID or name when several are open.

tools.name: check_tags
tools.description: QA check over the live document: paragraphs whose inline tag markers (..., ...) differ from the source – by count, or by tag name as a multiset when counts agree. Needs the Supervertaler preview tool running. A count difference can be legitimate; a name mismatch with equal counts rarely is.

document.description: Document GUID or name when several are open.

tools.name: check_nbsp
tools.description: QA check over the live document: translated paragraphs with fewer non-breaking spaces (U+00A0) than their source. Invisible on screen and in every tool response, so this is the only way to see a lost one – relevant where a style guide wants a non-breaking space between a value and its unit. Needs the Supervertaler preview tool running.

document.description: Document GUID or name when several are open.

tools.name: check_terminology
tools.description: QA check over the live document against the Supervertaler glossary: source paragraphs containing a glossary term whose target lacks the expected rendering (inflection tolerated), and any target using a term marked FORBIDDEN. Longest match wins where entries overlap. Needs the Supervertaler preview tool running and a glossary configured.

document.description: Document GUID or name when several are open.

tools.name: find_inconsistencies
tools.description: Find translation inconsistencies in the live document: repeated source paragraphs (compared tag-stripped) whose translations differ. Returns each group with its source and every occurrence (index, target). Needs the Supervertaler preview tool running. To align them, stage the preferred translation for the others and have the user Pre-translate, or point them there with go_to_segment.

document.description: Document GUID or name when several are open.

tools.name: get_confirmed_pairs
tools.description: Source/target pairs the translator has personally confirmed in this document, newest last. This is the gold standard: match their terminology and register in anything you stage. Requires the plugin to be selected under Self-learning MT in memoQ; if always empty, tell the user to check that setting.

document.description: Document key from get_project. Omit for the most recently active document.

tools.name: lookup_term
tools.description: Search the Supervertaler glossary for terms occurring in the given text. Returns each match with its approved target and whether it is forbidden. Forbidden terms must never appear in a translation, in any form.

text.description: Text to scan for glossary terms - a segment, a phrase, or a single word.

tools.name: add_term
tools.description: Add a term to the Supervertaler glossary. It appears in memoQ's terminology pane and is enforced in every later translation request within seconds. Set forbidden=true to ban a target term instead of approving one. Confirm with the user before adding terms they did not explicitly approve.

target.description: Approved target-language term (or the banned term when forbidden=true).

forbidden.description: True to mark the target as forbidden rather than preferred.

tools.name: stage_translations
tools.description: Stage translations for memoQ segments. NOTHING is written into memoQ by this call: staged pairs wait until the user runs Pre-translate or lands on the segment. PREFER partId: give the row's partId from get_segments and the plugin takes the source text from its own copy, so you never retype it - a source with one character wrong is accepted and then never matches anything. Without partId, matching is by source text and 'source' must be EXACTLY as get_segments returned it. BEWARE PARAGRAPHS: get_segments on a live document returns paragraphs, and memoQ asks for a translation per GRID ROW, per sentence. A paragraph memoQ splits matches nothing, whichever way you stage it - it also splits on abbreviations, so a short label can become two rows. For any job beyond a few dozen segments: stage a first pass, have the user run Pre-translate once, then read get_segments on the captured-requests document (the key in get_project whose origin is 'translation requests') which shows the EXACT strings memoQ asks for and which are already staged, stage what is missing, and run Pre-translate again. Reproduce whatever markup arrives in the source, byte for byte, wherever it belongs in the target. The forms depend on memoQ's import filter and vary between projects: and are common, ... and ... occur, and an HTML element can arrive as several spec_char tags rather than one. Placeholders are not consistent either - {0} may arrive as a tag while %1 arrives as literal text - so never normalise or rewrite markup, and never assume a form you have seen before. The reply reports pairs whose source matches nothing, tag differences, and trailing whitespace it adjusted; read it.

partId.description: The row's partId from get_segments. Strongly preferred: the plugin then quotes the source itself and no transcription can go wrong.

source.description: Segment source text, verbatim from get_segments. Ignored when partId is given.

target.description: Your translation, with the source's markup reproduced exactly.

label.description: Shown to the user as the origin of these translations (default "Claude").

tools.name: get_staged
tools.description: List what is staged, with how many times memoQ has pulled each one (timesServed > 0 means it reached the grid). Use neverServed=true after a Pre-translate to see only what did NOT land, and compact=true to leave out the targets you wrote yourself - the full list runs to six figures of characters on a real job and will overflow.

neverServed.description: Only pairs memoQ has never pulled.

sourceContains.description: Only pairs whose source contains this text.

compact.description: Leave out target, label and time.

tools.name: compare_staged_to_grid
tools.description: Did the staged translations land? Compares the live grid against everything staged and reports, per document and in total, how many rows carry the staged translation, how many differ, how many are EMPTY, and how many have nothing staged - then lists the problem rows. Ask this before telling the user a job is ready to confirm. An empty row with a translation staged for it is the shape of a Pre-translate that cleared it. Note it compares PARAGRAPHS, so a paragraph memoQ split into sentences reads as not staged even when its sentences were staged individually; the note in the reply says which case you are looking at.

document.description: One document key from get_project; omit for the whole project.

limit.description: At most this many problem rows (default 100, max 500).

tools.name: clear_staged
tools.description: Clear the staging area. Use when the user wants to start over, or after a job is delivered. Does not touch anything already pulled into memoQ.

tools.name: list_prompts
tools.description: List the prompts in the shared Supervertaler prompt library (name, path, category, description). The same library the Trados plugin and the prompt editor use.

tools.name: get_prompt
tools.description: Read one prompt's full content by its relative path (from list_prompts).

path.description: Relative path of the prompt, e.g. "Translate/Default/Default Translation Prompt.md".

tools.name: save_prompt
tools.description: Create or update a prompt in the shared Supervertaler library. Use this to draft a project-specific translation prompt from what get_project, get_segments, get_confirmed_pairs and lookup_term tell you - then the user selects it in memoQ under Resources > Settings > MT > Supervertaler > Prompt. A prompt with the same name and category is updated in place. Use {{SOURCE_LANGUAGE}} and {{TARGET_LANGUAGE}} placeholders rather than naming languages.

category.description: Library folder (default "Translate"). Must start with "Translate" to appear in memoQ's dropdown.

tools.name: list_supermemory_banks
tools.description: List the translator's memory banks - their own notes on a client: terminology decisions and the reasoning behind them, style rules, standing instructions. Call this FIRST when the user says something like "check the memory bank for this project", so you can name the right one. Do not guess a bank from the project name: each bank holds one client's conventions and the wrong one is worse than none. The bank named _shared is not a sibling - it layers underneath whichever bank you read and loses to it where they disagree.

tools.name: get_supermemory_context
tools.description: Read a memory bank as a formatted block: client brief, style rules and terminology decisions, with the _shared house defaults layered underneath. These are choices the translator made deliberately and cannot be derived from the source text, so contradicting one is an error rather than a stylistic difference. Use it before translating or advising on a project. The reply's "trimmed" list names anything that did not fit the token budget - if it is present you do NOT have the whole bank, and can ask again with a larger tokenBudget.

bank.description: Bank folder name, from list_supermemory_banks. An unknown name is an error rather than a silent fall back to another bank.

q.description: Optional. Bias retrieval towards this text, e.g. the term being asked about.

tokenBudget.description: Optional. Defaults to 6000, which is deliberately small because this answer stays in the conversation and is re-sent every turn. Raise it only when "trimmed" says you are missing something.

tools.name: search_supermemory
tools.description: Keyword-search a memory bank and the _shared overlay, returning scored snippets with their file paths. Use it to check whether the translator has already decided something - a term, a phrasing, a client preference - before you invent an answer. The reply lists which banks were searched: no hits means it is not written down in those banks, which is different from it not mattering.
